author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1847
status: 여름철새 수만 마리 · 나그네새 수천 마리
summary: 산지 저지대 낙엽활엽수림에 사는 새로, 우리나라에서는 흔한 나그네새이며, 해마다 수만 마리가 찾아와 번식하는 여름철새이기도 하다. 혼자 또는 암수가 함께 지내고 무리를 짓지 않는다. 낙엽활엽수림이나 관목림의 풀뿌리, 땅 위, 벼랑의 오목한 곳에 이끼, 나무껍질, 낙엽으로 둥근 둥지를 짓고, 5~6월에 흰 알을 4~6개 낳는다. 히말라야에서 중앙아시아를 거쳐 중국 북동부와 일본까지 분포하며, 겨울에는 남쪽으로 내려간다.

art.subject: Eastern Crowned Warbler (Phylloscopus coronatus), adult (sexes alike), as seen in Korean deciduous forest from May to August: crown dark olive with a pale greyish-white median crown stripe from the forehead to the nape; long yellowish-white supercilium; dark olive eye-stripe; upperparts bright olive-green; wings olive with one faint narrow yellowish wing-bar; underparts silky dull white, at most faintly yellow-tinged on the belly centre, with clearly pale yellow undertail coverts. Bill fairly large for a leaf warbler: upper mandible dark brown, lower mandible entirely pale orange-yellow. Dark eye. Brownish legs.
art.pose: foraging alone among the leaves of a deciduous tree, side view
art.scene: Korean lowland deciduous broadleaf forest at the foot of a mountain in late spring; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a twig: pale median crown stripe between dark olive crown sides, yellowish-white supercilium, dark eye-stripe, olive-green upperparts with one faint wing-bar, dull white underparts with a faint yellow belly centre, pale yellow undertail coverts, brownish legs

adult, head detail from above and slightly to the side: pale central crown stripe from forehead to nape bordered by dark olive lateral crown stripes; dark brown upper and pale orange-yellow lower mandible
art.build: Small leaf warbler, a little smaller than a sparrow and slimmer, with a relatively large head and long bill for its group; slim and active, usually in the mid-canopy. Bill thin, straight, pointed, a little shorter than the head, with a wholly pale lower mandible. Legs medium length, brownish. Wings fairly long and pointed. Tail medium length, square to slightly notched. Constantly moving, often flicking its wings.
avoid: Do not paint a plain, unstriped crown; the pale central crown stripe is the key mark (Arctic Warbler lacks it).
Do not paint two bold white wing-bars or a yellow rump (Pallas's Leaf Warbler).
Do not paint a yellow throat and breast; the clearly yellow part is the undertail coverts.
Do not paint an all-dark bill.
